newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peru's Fujimori says crisis can be solved.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori says crisis can be solved.

text.p: Peru's President Alberto Fujimori said on Tuesday the Lima hostage crisis could be resolved without violence but said the Marxist hostage-takers must lay down their arms and free the 83 people they are holding.

"I believe that in the end reason will impose a solution without the spilling of blood, fully respectful of the human rights of the hostages and hostage-takers," Fujimori told the Spanish news agency EFE.

In the interview, made available to Reuters in Madrid, Fujimori reiterated that while the government was keeping up dialogue with the hostage-takers it ruled out "any possibility of freeing the jailed militants of the MRTA" -- one of the guerrillas' original demands.
Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels seized the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima in a spectacular raid on December 17.

The guerrillas have freed more than 420 hostages since they took over the building, but 83 remain captive, including three ambassadors, dozens of Japanese businessmen and most senior officials from Peru's police and intelligence forces.
